# Requirement-to-test inventory

**Behavioral authority:** `documentation/specification/2026-10-21 - specification handoff.md`, consolidated 2026-10-21, at commit `7870042a02e094dca772d6fdd6570ad7b2d02578`.
**Organizational authority:** `documentation/specification/2026-10-21 - test suite structure.md`, v2, same commit.
**Provenance:** user-approved six-wave plan. Wave 1 was expressly authorized; forwarded independent OK verdicts successively authorized Waves 2–6 and final reconciliation. No subsequent Architect decision is used.
**Review status:** Waves 1/2/3 accepted by forwarded independent OK verdicts for `7364ed8843c565592d4bfa550d90c218988c83ba`, `196d16b056668f3292e8309d545e6aaa49c90497` and `f915ba0a3aaee70588fe115d23d992242180c226`, each verified reachable from remote main. Wave 4 received forwarded independent OK for fe3eba9f46612f927c74edf52a62cdee6cb69365, verified reachable from remote main. Wave 5 received forwarded independent OK for `786c91b8f8e446d8d67709c79f8923d600204056`, verified reachable from remote main. Wave 6 received the forwarded independent OK for `5076be06f1f3c21e408abbed385ef93985794f44`; its effective-configuration correction received the forwarded independent OK for `7d1035cc746bbe381a4c0b436012fd07b8b97721`, verified on remote main. All six waves and their latest corrections are accepted. Final reconciliation is complete within the accepted testable scope, subject to the explicit clarification and execution limits below.

## Status meanings and evidence limits

- **Implemented / integration unavailable:** real executable assertions exist at the exact node IDs below. All 2335 conversion/control cases currently fail with `ImplementationUnavailable` because no verified production implementation/API exists. No transformation assertion has passed or been certified by this run.
- **Harness only / passed:** 88 independent fixture/RDF-helper checks passed. They are listed separately and receive no DirectKG transformation coverage credit.
- **Planned:** later-wave assertions are not implemented merely because they appear here.
- **Blocked for clarification:** the affected exact expectation has no normative answer; independent assertions continue. No skip/xfail hides this status.

The observed run collected 2425 cases: 88 fixture/helper checks and 2 read-only vocabulary checks passed; 2335 failed at the integration boundary, no skips/xfails or collection errors. No other failure class was observed. See `tests/README.md` for reproducible commands and binding boundaries. This is assertion traceability, not a line-coverage metric or a claim of exhaustive inputs.

Rule IDs in each implemented test's `Rules:` docstring match its inventory references. Exact sections supplement IDs for unnumbered clauses. Each parameter row is explicit below. Runtime mutations start from the complete listed source and are written to pytest temporary files; these are reviewed case edits, not simplified replacement export schemas or a fixture-builder framework. No generated runtime output belongs in fixture directories.

Earlier Wave 1 self-check correction (`12f7906`): generic attribute missing-name diagnostics (DK-IRI-04)
and the integrated extensionality INFO (DK-DIAG-17) check identification of the
affected declaration through any unambiguous actually reported locator. They do
not require a literal source ID where the rule does not mandate one. The binding
records this identification separately from explicitly reported IDs; class-fallback
and duplicate-ID assertions retain their explicit-ID requirements. The ordinary
ID-use case also rejects forbidden missing-name events independently of locator
format. Node IDs, fixture pairings, and approved wave scope are unchanged.

Wave 1 reviewer correction (F1–F3): identifier destinations are established
without reading the identifier under test; reused files are promoted to canonical
shared bundles with every consumer/pairing updated; and a two-declaration input
with IDs `"C17"` and `" C17 "` exercises exact comparison without trimming under
all three input policies. Existing node IDs are preserved, including harness
IDs for promoted inputs. Only the four new cases listed below are added.

## Fixture provenance and contract checks

All stored source models are purpose-authored to the inspected **ontouml-vp-plugin 0.5.3** structure, not claimed to be literal exports from a running VP installation. The official release resolves to commit `9fc02b8162db9910f21b8713549cafce2627dad0`:
<https://github.com/OntoUML/ontouml-vp-plugin/tree/9fc02b8162db9910f21b8713549cafce2627dad0>.

Inspected files under `src/main/java/it/unibz/inf/ontouml/vp/model/` establish the used shapes:

| Used structure | 0.5.3 evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Project/model root, nesting, identifiers | `vp2ontouml/IProjectTransformer.java`; `ontouml/serialization/ProjectSerializer.java`, `PackageSerializer.java`, `ElementSerializer.java`, `ModelElementSerializer.java` |
| Classifier/property fields, explicit false/nulls, reference objects | `ontouml/serialization/ClassSerializer.java`, `ClassifierSerializer.java`, `RelationSerializer.java`, `PropertySerializer.java`, `Serializer.java`, `DecoratableSerializer.java` |
| Plain text and bounded localized carrier interpretation | `ontouml/serialization/MultilingualTextSerializer.java`; RD-27 in the normative baseline. No newer document structure is used by these fixtures. |
| Custom tag value shapes and dedicated-field separation | `vp2ontouml/ITaggedValueTransformer.java`; custom strings/numbers/booleans are used. Built-in `isExtensional` is supplied as its dedicated class field, not as a custom tag. |
| Diagram owner/contents, class/relation views, rectangles, routed paths | `ontouml/serialization/DiagramSerializer.java`, `DiagramElementSerializer.java`, `NodeViewSerializer.java`, `ClassViewSerializer.java`, `ConnectorViewSerializer.java`, `RelationViewSerializer.java`, `ShapeSerializer.java`, `RectangularShapeSerializer.java`, `PathSerializer.java` |
| Explicit generalization reference fields | `ontouml/serialization/GeneralizationSerializer.java` and actual Catalog examples |
| Recognized class-stereotype spellings in corrected Wave 4 mode inputs | `ontouml/model/ClassStereotype.java` at the pinned 0.5.3 commit declares `MODE("mode")`; the positive mode cases use `require-known`. No custom alias supplies intrinsic/extrinsic semantics. |

The Catalog files `OntoUML/ontouml-models/models/library/ontology.json` (blob `0ef9f0b0543eb31035489907160d9759c6166d45`) and `models/guizzardi2005ontological/ontology.json` (blob `8d48eac24e8bb451893ec136be1bb2f366edb28e`) corroborated nested Package contents, complete Class/Property/Relation variants, null fields, and `{id,type}` references. Their top-level data did **not** declare an exporter version. No raw Catalog file was copied into this suite or certified as a 0.5.3 fixture.

There are 41 stored JSON sources: 31 contract-positive cases (including the explicit no-validation-of-omitted-view-IDs case), 9 parseable governed negatives (2 unknown-information cases, 7 duplicate-declaration cases), and 1 intentionally malformed JSON document. The exact-ID-comparison positive reuses the inspected complete Project/Package/Class fields and has two category classes with IDs `"C17"` and `" C17 "`; it introduces no new exporter structure. Fixture checks verify the named authoring defects, reference/type resolution, binary ends, and the presentation structures used here. They are bounded authoring checks, not a production validator or a compatibility claim for arbitrary schema documents.

Ten stored Turtle files are partial ground asserted graphs. The additional relations/material_pattern/expected_chain.ttl is an ordered chain with an anonymous inverse expression; tests compare its actual property-expression sequence, not blank-node identifiers. Their exact input/expectation pairing is recorded below, including cross-bundle use of the canonical shared core. Unknown concrete DKGM identity, optional metadata, and unspecified generated-comment wording prevent a whole-output fixture from being normative. Inter-conversion comparisons select fixed domain predicates, retain required source labels/IDs, and permit the stated unordered pairwise disjointness presentation. Serialization round trips and access within the same conversion use whole-graph isomorphism. None of these checks requires an OWL reasoner, textual Turtle order, stable blank-node labels or byte-identical output.

Equivalent cases are grouped deliberately: the complete stereotype table is tested with default tolerant input handling, with selected cells repeated under all input policies to establish precedence. Every-policy repetition is retained for explicit policy-independent fatal/nonfatal guarantees. Ordinary collision suffix allocation is checked as a complete suffix set and repeated source mapping; ID ordering is not invented where the rule leaves it open.

Runtime negative mutations retain the full exporter structure and introduce only
the stated defect. Independent harness checks cover invalid literal IDs/lists,
unresolved refs, and source traversal. Audit-only malformed language/categorizer
cases do not assert production recovery where the specification leaves it open.
OWL2 permits `owl:members` and `owl:distinctMembers` on AllDifferent; the helper
accepts both, arbitrary collection order, equivalent anonymous enumeration
expressions, and multiple groups establishing all required distinct pairs.
See the primary [OWL2 RDF mapping](https://www.w3.org/TR/owl2-mapping-to-rdf/).
It rejects missing membership or improper closure without simulating a converter.

Wave 2 deliberately groups equivalent cases: one hierarchy-free stereotype
matrix covers every required/forbidden pair; member counts and flags isolate
coverage/disjointness branches; all input policies are repeated for explicit
fatal/nonfatal guarantees. The language precedence matrix is shared across
source names/descriptions; representative class/attribute/value paths exercise
each selector boundary, while all 16 supported entity/end text paths exercise
placement and lexical preservation. This avoids a redundant product of every
stereotype, text field, language context, and policy. Flag-comment wording is
unfixed, so actual RDF comments are read through test-side semantic observations,
with their exact subject/literal verified, rather than an invented message template.

Wave 3 uses the user-approved **Attributes, datatypes, property references,
and source flags** scope, authorized by the forwarded Wave 2 OK. Five additional
purpose-authored complete JSON models and two partial ground RDF expectations
bring stored data to 34 JSON and 7 Turtle files (41 exact paths). They use the
same pinned VP-plugin 0.5.3 source, commit
`9fc02b8162db9910f21b8713549cafce2627dad0`. Newly re-inspected sources under
`src/main/java/it/unibz/inf/ontouml/vp/model/` are:

- `ontouml/serialization/PropertySerializer.java`: boolean flags, nullable
  cardinality string/type reference, Property-reference arrays, aggregation name.
- `ontouml/model/Property.java`: Property references, attributes versus ends,
  class/relation target types and aggregation fields.
- `vp2ontouml/IPropertyTransformer.java`: multiplicity copied from exporter,
  actual subsetting/redefinition iteration and SHARED/COMPOSITE/NONE extraction.

No raw Catalog export is newly claimed or copied. Language carriers remain the
bounded previously verified enrichment. Stored inputs are contract-positive;
invalid cardinalities/reference mutations retain complete source structure and
are checked for their stated authoring defects. No runtime fixture-builder
framework, production mapping, new dependency/configuration or path exception is
introduced. Cardinality fixtures remain topic-owned until another behavioral
module actually consumes them. RDF helper samples receive no conversion credit.

Equivalent cases are grouped: primitive registry/safety boundaries use bounded
representatives; all policies repeat null/missing/invalid and contradiction
rules; field/direction/inverse-availability axes cover independent property
expressions without a Cartesian product of labels/stereotypes. Flag contexts
are read from actual comments, with exact RDF evidence and diagnostic meanings.
Extra prohibited flag-induced logical/sequence output is read through the
replaceable observation boundary, never manufactured from expectations. All 682
previous IDs remain; Wave 3 adds 327 behavioral and 13 harness locations.

Wave 4 is authorized by the forwarded OK for `f915ba0a3aaee70588fe115d23d992242180c226`.
It adds four purpose-authored full JSON models and two explicitly paired partial
Turtle expectations using the already inspected 0.5.3 Property/Relation,
Generalization/GeneralizationSet and reference structures. No new exporter or
schema support is inferred. `shared/binary_relation` is canonical from first use
by relations and inverses. The formerly property-owned connector input is
promoted byte-for-byte to `shared/omitted_connector`; all consumers and records
are updated and its previous harness node ID is retained. No existing attribute
JSON is consumed by another topic, so those inputs stay in their owning bundles.

The two new modules use the existing generic RDF readers; expected relation
cardinality forms remain local to relation assertions. Interface observation
fields for actual fallback-origin markers, multi-member coverage substitutes and
inverse-omission report entries require an audited real binding. The public
Python-control query imposes no production signature and fails explicitly while
unbound. No diagnostic/comment/report observation may be manufactured.

Equivalent cases are grouped: the 30-row naming matrix has 18 exact
role-resolvable assertions, 10 bounded-candidate assertions whose exact choice
is blocked below, and two externalDependence cases with only independent mapping
assertions pending clarification of the accepted mode-role encoding. Representative precedence/label cases avoid a stereotype ×
label × language product. Cardinality recovery repeats every policy and both end
directions; named-inverse recovery is sampled separately from the exhaustive
anonymous recovery matrix. Independent flags/inverse availability, surviving
explicit specifics and required source-end ordering retain their material combinations.
The Wave 4 self-check adds the two one-sided inverse-disjointness cases; both
inverses present and both absent remain covered by the independent flag matrix.
All 1022 previously approved node IDs remain; Wave 4 adds 633 behavioral and 9
harness cases, for 1664 total. Its full-suite failures are integration failures,
not evidence that transformation or semantic readers executed successfully.

Wave 5 extends the approved relation/property/ontology/higher-order modules and
the existing generic RDF reader/invocation boundary. Three purpose-authored full
VP-plugin 0.5.3-shaped models add no exporter support:

- `tests/fixtures/shared/material_pattern/input.json` — canonical from first use across relations and properties; explicitly paired with `tests/fixtures/transformation/relations/material_pattern/expected_chain.ttl` only for its stated ID-mode/default-direction chain.
- `tests/fixtures/transformation/relations/chain_constraints/input.json` — relation hierarchy, singleton completeness, disjointness and numeric restrictions around one actual chain.
- `tests/fixtures/shared/instantiation/input.json` — explicit instantiation declaration plus independent categorizers.

The serializer/reference structures and recognized mode spelling reuse the pinned
0.5.3 evidence above. Grounding endpoints use actual Relation/Class reference
variants. The runtime broken-endpoint cases are intentional governed invalid
inputs; matching uses IDs, not source-name or serialization heuristics.
No prior fixture is newly consumed outside its owning topic unless already shared.
The plan's old root vocabulary resource now resides in canonical latest/versioned
locations under vocabulary/; both actual files are read without modification.
No test artifact changes location and no structural exception is introduced.

Instantiation provenance variants inspect actual programmatic graphs only.
File delivery/export schemas, thresholds and exit codes are implemented in Wave 6. New
semantic readers for actual omitted-connector output, comparative additions and
discarded instantiation values default to unbound None and must explicitly observe
an empty tuple. No empty result may be manufactured from a requested policy.

All 1664 previously approved node IDs remain. Wave 5 adds 410 integration-bound
assertions, 2 passing existing-resource assertions and 5 passing harness checks.
No passing resource or helper check certifies unavailable conversion/readers.

## Blockers, exclusions, and placement reconciliation

- **Blocked for Architect clarification:** DK-GEN-04's concrete stable `U` is
  unspecified. The existing vocabulary URI is not substituted for an accepted
  decision. Import-shape assertions do not certify its exact identity or contents.
- **Blocked for Architect clarification — semantic directional roles in DK-REL-04:**
  The table distinguishes whole/component (`componentOf`), dependent/antecedent
  (`historicalDependence`), part/whole event (`participational`), and sub/super
  collection or quantity (`subCollectionOf`, `subQuantityOf`). It does not state
  which supported source fields establish those roles. DK-REL-06 says it
  "assumes valid relation orientation"; DK-PROP-04 forbids using source flags to
  reverse/normalize direction or infer additional semantics. Class names in
  authored fixtures are labels, not an authorized semantic-role convention.
  Targeted decision: which supported input fields determine these five rows'
  directional roles for lexical naming? Ten table cases assert only one of the
  established row candidates and retain explicit primary direction, not an
  invented exact directional choice. Eighteen direction cells are exact.
- **F1 correction / blocked for Architect clarification — externalDependence mode role:**
  The pinned exporter `ClassStereotype.java` establishes `mode`, not separate
  intrinsic/extrinsic stereotype aliases. DK-REL-04 names "Extrinsic Mode" while
  DK-REL-07/08 explicitly use `«mode»` for material-mode patterns; neither states
  a supported-field criterion for the former role. The two corrected cells use
  `mode`/`kind` with require-known and assert only completion and primary
  identity/domain/range. They assert no lexical candidate or naming-diagnostic
  silence and do not claim DK-REL-04 coverage. Targeted Architect decision:
  does a recognized `mode` endpoint on `externalDependence` establish that role
  for naming, or which supported field does? No clarification has been received.
  Characterization/manifestation use the accepted `mode` spelling for their
  feature/aspect input; both material-mode dependencies likewise use `mode`.
- **F2 reviewer correction:** DK-REL-15 and DK-GEN-02 select successfully mapped
  explicit specific relations for disjointness, independently of a failed
  general property or general reference. Four best-effort variants retain the
  Middle/Sibling primary pair and its named-inverse pair when both inverses
  exist; hierarchy omissions and the prohibition on singleton coverage remain.
- **Wave 4 known auxiliary-name boundary:** unusable-but-present role values and
  unusable inverse-domain qualifiers retain eligible, distinct, correctly
  directed inverse properties and labels/source identity. Exact final auxiliary
  names remain blocked under DK-INV-05/06/08 and DK-IRI-10, as in the approved plan.
- **Wave 4 scope/placement reconciliation:** two new topical modules, four full
  JSON models and two partial RDF expectations; one canonical input promotion;

  and this single inventory. All 1022 prior IDs are preserved. No new helper
